newsitem.title: UK: Flat panel TVs offer outdoor advertising potential.
newsitem.headline: Flat panel TVs offer outdoor advertising potential.

text.p: New flat panel televisions with screens no thicker than a couple of hardback books offer a new opportunity in outdoor advertising, allowing bus shelter advertising panels which could be changed throughout the day.

Japanese electronics giant NEC Corp earlier this week said it has begun selling the world's thinnest television, with a picture quality matching that of ordinary TVs. NEC said its new television, called Plasma X, is a mere 99 millimetres wide, including power supply, tuner and speakers. Ordinary 42-inch TVs measure are about one metre wide because they use bulky cathode ray tubes.
"At some point in the next five or six years that screen will become economical on bus shelters," Roger Parry, chief executive of More Group Plc, told Reuters on Friday.
More Group, Britain's largest outdoor advertising company, is a major player in the sale of advertising panels on bus shelters.

"When it falls below $10,000 per shelter it becomes economic," Parry said of the potential of the new flat panel televisions. He expects the $10,000 benchmark will be reached in the next five to 10 years.

The new televisions offer not just a physical size compatible with bus shelter advertising panels, but also offer better picture resolution. Existing widescreen televisions offer good picture resolution for night-time viewing of bus shelter ads, but the daytime quality remains poor, Parry said.

Television screen advertising in the outdoor market likely would continue to use static, rather than moving images. But the technology would allow for optical fibre links to remote studios, meaning that ads at each bus shelter could be changed throughout the day.
Ads might be changed up to five times a day to target changing audiences, such as morning and evening commuters, Parry said.
"Advertisers will pay a significant premium for that," he said.
